location.region: Anxi (historical origin; today the style is more widely produced in Taiwan)

description.short: The least oxidized oolong, rivaling green tea in freshness while offering superior aromatic complexity
description.overview: Occupies a unique middle ground between green tea and classic oolongs: minimal oxidation preserves the crisp liveliness of green tea, while the oolong bruising process yields deep floral sophistication.
description.leaf: Gently twisted into loose open strips (not rolled into balls), dark-green leaves
description.aroma: Fresh floral, reminiscent of delicate orchids and vibrant spring greens
description.taste: Light, clean, delicately sweet, with virtually no astringency
description.processing: Plucking → withering → gentle tossing/shaking for minimal edge oxidation → fixation (kill-green) → gentle rolling into loose strips (no ball shaping) → drying without roasting

history.origin: The name translates to 'wrapped kind'—historically, the finished tea was wrapped and sold in square paper parcels, which gave the tea its distinctive moniker.
history.development: Originally developed in Fujian, the technique was brought to northern Taiwan in the 19th century by Fujianese immigrants, where Bao Zhong (widely known as Pouchong) flourished into a signature regional craft.
history.modern: Today, Taiwanese Wenshan Pouchong is often regarded as the benchmark of this style, though the original methods and roots remain firmly rooted in mainland Fujian.
interestingFacts: Bao Zhong is widely known as a 'bridge tea' between green and oolong teas—its light oxidation places it closer to green tea than any other oolong variety.
The signature square paper parcel packaging historically set it apart from ordinary teas sold strictly in bulk bins.
